analysis.investment_thesis: Bandhan Bank is a turnaround story — profits recovered from a dismal INR 126 Cr in FY22 to INR 2,745 Cr in FY25, and the forward P/E of 10.92 against P/B of just 1.14 suggests the stock is priced for continued stress rather than recovery. The problem is that revenue grew only 7.8% CAGR and the microfinance book remains fragile in an stressed rural credit environment.
key_strengths: Forward P/E of 10.92 and P/B of 1.14 offer a margin of safety if the earnings recovery is genuine
Net profit has compounded strongly off a depressed FY22 base, reaching 2,745 Cr in FY25
Debt reduction on the funding side (borrowings down from 24,711 Cr to 11,138 Cr) and cash build shows balance sheet discipline
key_risks: Revenue (net interest income + fees) CAGR of only 7.8% over 3 years — far too slow for a growth bank story
Finance costs grew 26.6% CAGR, rising faster than revenue — liability repricing squeezes margins
ROE of only 11.16% sits below my 12% minimum and hasn't sustainably crossed that threshold
red_flags: MFI/microfinance sector in India facing elevated delinquencies — Bandhan's east India concentration amplifies this risk
Operating cash flow was deeply negative in FY23 (-4,245 Cr) and erratic — bank-level OCF is inherently volatile but the swings are wide
Current P/E of 27.92 on trailing earnings looks expensive; the forward P/E thesis depends heavily on a sharp earnings re-acceleration that isn't yet proven
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Lynch would tag Bandhan as a turnaround — the question is whether the turn is real and durable or just a cyclical respite from a bad MFI vintage. The bank has genuinely cleaned up its balance sheet (borrowings nearly halved), and the FY25 profit of 2,745 Cr is encouraging. But the forward P/E of 10.92 only looks cheap if you trust that number — and with MFI stress still unresolved across the sector, I'm skeptical of the trajectory.

The core problem for a Lynch investor is the growth rate. At 7.8% revenue CAGR, this isn't the kind of small bank that grows 20%+ and takes market share. Bandhan was once that story; today it's a recovery narrative at a bank that has narrowed its ambitions. At P/B of 1.14 the downside is limited but I don't see a ten-bagger here — hold for those already in, but not compelling enough to buy fresh.
